correctness.rationale: Lucas parity identifies each Pascal row modulo two with submasks D(s). For s<t, |D(s)△D(t)|≥2^{max(h(s),h(t))−1}, so independent elliptic Bernoulli coefficients yield |E[f(s)f(t)]|≤(1−2ε)^{2^{h(t)−1}}. Grouping by bit-count up to 2^L gives total upper bound exp(C(log(L+2))²). Dyadic aligned-block decomposition bounds the maximal spatial prefix second moment by 2^L exp(C(log(L+2))²); dyadic Markov–Borel–Cantelli provides the asserted sqrtN exp(C(loglogN)²) a.s. spatial rate. The monotone count S_n has independent geometric(1/2) holding lengths; centered weighted lengths are a martingale, controlled uniformly by Doob and Borel–Cantelli, and the incomplete holding and ζ0 convention are negligible. Therefore the actual predictable off-diagonal bracket has the same a.s. quenched bound. For independent fair β, invertible lower-triangular Pascal transform yields iid fair f(s); independent geometric holding times have EH=2 and EH²=6, so renewal-reward CLT gives variance3 and proves polynomial exponent 1/2 optimal uniformly over the admitted family. Independently verified 8,128 distinct submask distance bounds and bijections of every fair Pascal transform through size8.

Related qualitative static quenched limits and fair-profile Brownian fluctuations are acknowledged; the novel assessed result is the near-square-root uniform almost-sure maximal bracket estimate across arbitrary heterogeneous elliptic parameters. Earlier abstract Walsh/Pascal maximal estimates could imply this without matching nomenclature and remain a serious priority risk.

value.rationale: A near-optimal almost-sure all-prefix rate for predictable cross-bracket, uniform across independent but arbitrarily nonstationary elliptic scenery, is mathematically significant for quantitative martingale covariance control; the fair case proves its polynomial exponent cannot improve uniformly. Unlike qualitative o(N) strong law, this gives a controlled Brownian-scale error.

limitations: Requires independent static elliptic Bernoulli coefficients and fair driving signs; no sharp subpolynomial factor and no nonfair or dependent environments.
